evidence: sheets/<id>.png (row 1 desktop start/mid/finish/reveal, row 2 phone), native-resolution desktop stage crops and 2x phone zooms (/tmp/quality/b4/*.png), metrics.json, catalog_A rows, CREATIVE_STANDARDS.md
shared_findings: Phone (all 14 games): the header title is clipped to 'MOTIONAL RELEASE CONSO' and the LVL pill sits on top of it. The mic icon covers the end of the input text ('my boss yelled at me an[mic]e').

Eight of the 14 games (42, 45, 46, 47, 49, 51, 52, 53) are built from one template: a large rounded glass stage panel holding a dark word card of about 120 px. The card has a character sticker of about 25 px inside a dark capsule chip, with the word below. The chip is a dark box around the circular face, which fails the bubble rule. The sticker changes emotion from word to word but never reacts. Three more games (44, 48, 54) use the same panel, empty, with the word as text of about 9 px in the middle.

Look-alike gestures in the Detach cluster: 44 VELCRO, 45 MAGNETS, 47 UNFOLLOW and 49 UNZIP all finish with the same gesture, dragging one object to the right past a threshold (a patch, an orb, a plug, a zipper pull). 46 is drag up and 48 is drag diagonal. This breaks creative standard 3.

Every game that finishes ends on the same reveal card ('RELEASE COMPLETE / NAME / STEADIER ✓ … / FEEL A SHIFT?') over an empty backdrop. The tilted 'RELEASED · SHIFT COMPLETE / LESS GRIP. MORE STILL.' card appears in the desktop finish tiles of 45 and 49 and the phone finish of 50. The only impact effect is one white centre-flash blob, identical in every game (42 mid, 43 finish, 46 finish, 50 mid, 53 mid and finish). In the phone mid tiles of 40, 42, 46, 49, 52, 53 and 54, the '+STILL HIT · CHAIN ×N' toast covers the object being played.

Functional failures: 45 phone stalls at 17% because the orb never respawns after round 1. 47 phone stalls at 0% because dragging selects the image and the text instead of moving a plug about 6 px wide. 48 stalls at 50% on both sizes. 51 stalls at 25% on both sizes. 42 desktop needed 66 s to finish, and its reveal was not captured.

The HUD contradicts itself. In the 53 and 54 phone finish tiles the counter reads '2/6' and the bar is about 17% filled while the label says 'GAME PROGRESS · 100%'. 40 finishes on '4/6' and 43 on '5/6 CUT' with the label at 100%. The game appears to end before all six words are played.

Perf: under headless software rendering every game exceeds p95 > 34 ms and max > 120 ms. The batch sits below the fleet medians (phone p95 433 ms, desktop p95 783 ms). Relative outliers: a 1528 ms long task on 50 desktop, 4.25 s of long tasks on 45 desktop (max 764 ms), a 748 ms long task on 49 desktop, and desktop p95 of about 870-900 ms on 40, 52 and 54. Heap growth stays at or below 5.8 MB, and there are no errors.

games.name: PAPER PLANE
games.character_role: None in the world. The only character art is the faint, blurred ambient decals at the stage corners (phone start tile, top-left and right). No character folds the plane, rides it, throws it or watches it go.
games.finale: Phone finish tile: the plane slides off to the right and is cut off by the stage edge, with a 'STILL +1' toast in the centre and the counter on '4/6'. Then the shared reveal card ('PANIC ↓ YOU CREATED DISTANCE'). There is no sky, no flight path and none of the wind drift the catalog promises. Flying off-screen is a game-specific beat, but it is tiny and clipped, and the reveal is generic.
games.score_rationale: A4: the plane is a flat pale-cyan polygon with no paper grain, crease shading or shadow, floating on the shared nebula and ring backdrop (phone start, desktop start crop). B3: the plane is its own prop, but the world is the same nebula as every other game; there is no sky, desk or window. C4: fold ×2 then swipe is a good craft-then-release arc, but the mid tile shows a hard snap from W to triangle with no fold animation, and the toast covers the fold point. D1: decals only. E3: the fly-off exists but is clipped (phone finish), then the shared card. G4: the action button is big and readable, but the word printed on the plane is about 7 px with a grey text-shadow box (phone mid zoom), the plane is clipped at the right edge at finish, and the header is clipped. H5: letting go of a paper plane suits sadness and regret, but with no flight or distance the release is not felt.

games.strengths: The clearest two-step instruction in the batch: a large, readable 'THOUGHT MOVE · FOLD LEFT WING' button (phone start) and the 'Fold. Flick. Fly.' guide. The craft-then-release arc fits the theme, and the session is short (about 14 s on phone).
games.problems: Phone start and mid: the user's word on the plane ('my boss') is about 7 px and unreadable. Phone mid: the toast covers the fold. Phone finish: the plane is clipped by the right edge of the stage, the counter reads '4/6' while the label says 100%, and the guide's 'How to play' row is blank. improvements: Build a real flight finale: on the swipe, the camera pulls back into a warm sunset sky and the plane rides a curved arc with a wind wobble and a contrail. It shrinks to a glinting dot over a horizon, and the sky warms from dusk blue to gold. Keep the plane fully on screen until the camera hands off.

Make a sad character the pilot: it sits on the paper, slumped. Each fold makes it brace and squash. On the flick it leans forward (anticipation), whoops as the plane launches, and lets go of a little cloud of its sadness, which drifts off separately and fades, while the character waves and then smiles.
Animate the folds as real paper: a 250 ms crease rotation with a moving highlight along the fold line, a soft shadow under the plane, paper grain, and a crinkle sound on each fold.
Print the user's word on the wing at 15 px or more in a handwritten style, with no grey box. Move the toast above the plane.
Use all six words: one plane per word, with the earlier planes visible as dots on the horizon, so the counter and the bar stay in step.

improvements: Rebuild it as a real untangle: draw three soft yarn ropes knotted around the character, using verlet rope physics. Make the overwhelmed character the one tied up: at first it is squeezed and its eyes swirl. Each loosened knot lets it breathe out (a scale pulse), and with the last knot it stretches its arms, free.
Give it its own finale: the freed ropes unwind into a single smooth thread that draws a calm spiral and then a heart around the character, with warm light blooming through.
Highlight the live knot with a pulsing glow and a drag-direction arrow. Remove the fixed order, or show it plainly.

Put an overthinking character on the ring: it runs around it like a hamster wheel, faster with each word, panting. Each cut slows it, and on the last cut the loop straightens into a path it walks off along, smiling.
Give it its own finale: the severed ring unrolls into a straight horizon line and dawn light rises behind it. The orbs turn into calm stars.

improvements: Redesign for safety first: replace free typing with tap-to-pick catastrophe steps (pre-written, mild). The game then visualises the chain as a rope bridge stretching further from the solid ground of 'what actually happened', and the player taps 'walk back' to return step by step, so the arc ends on fact, not fear.

Have an anxious character walk the chain: it tiptoes further out on each 'and then', the planks get thinner and the character trembles. On the way back it regains footing, puffs out its chest on solid ground and relaxes.
Give it its own finale: the far-flung 'and then' planks dissolve into mist, and a warm spotlight lands on the single true first sentence, which glows solid while the character sits on it calmly.
On phone, put the action button above the Live Guide, keep every user-word row at 15 px or more, and do not let the result card overlap the guide.
